anchorEmpty: No usable trust anchors. Create one first.
anchorHelp: The CA the device certificates must chain to. A device earmarked for this profile takes its token from the certificate's common name: {{prefix}} followed by the CN, which is the device's external id.
authHelp_CERTIFICATE: Devices register with a client certificate whose chain reaches a trust anchor. There is no secret to issue or rotate.
authHelp_SECRET: Devices register with the provision key and a secret the server generates and shows once.
credentialAnchorHelp: The CA the certificate's chain must reach, now and at every connect. Only enabled, unexpired anchors are offered.
credentialCapReached: This device already holds {{max}} certificate credentials, the most it may hold. Remove one to add another.
credentialLegacy: A certificate credential with no trust anchor. It cannot authenticate; remove it and add it again.
credentialPemHelp: The device's certificate, optionally followed by the intermediates that link it to the trust anchor. The chain is verified now; one that could not authenticate is refused. Certificates only, never a private key.
deleteBlocked: This trust anchor cannot be deleted while it is in use: {{credentials}} credential(s) and {{profiles}} provisioning profile(s) still name it. Remove or re-point them first, or disable the anchor to stop trusting it.
deleteConfirm: Delete trust anchor “{{token}}”? This cannot be undone.
disableConfirm: Disable “{{name}}”? Every device whose certificate chains to it stops authenticating and is disconnected now, and cannot reconnect until the anchor is enabled again. {{credentials}} credential(s) and {{profiles}} provisioning profile(s) rely on it.
disabledNotice: This anchor is disabled. No certificate chaining to it authenticates, and the devices that relied on it are disconnected.
earmarkDerivedHint: This is a certificate profile: the device's token is derived from its certificate's common name as {{prefix}} followed by the CN. Set the external id to the CN and leave the token empty, or set it to that value.
errConflict: A trust anchor with this token or this certificate already exists.
errInUse: This trust anchor is still in use by a credential or a provisioning profile, so it cannot be deleted. Remove or re-point them first, or disable the anchor instead.
errNotFound: The trust anchor, or the device, could not be found. It may have been removed.
expiryChainHint: The earliest expiry across the certificate and the chain to its anchor
inUseNote: The credential count includes removed credentials the platform still holds, as they also block deletion.
listDescription: The certificate authorities this tenant trusts to vouch for its devices' client certificates
listEmpty: No trust anchors yet. Add the CA certificate that signs your devices' certificates to let them connect with a client certificate.
pemEmpty: Paste a certificate or choose a file.
pemHelp: Exactly one CA certificate: a root, or an intermediate to trust one sub-CA only. Paste it or choose the file. Certificates only, never a private key. It cannot be changed afterwards; another CA is another anchor.
pemLooksLikeKey: That text contains a private key. Remove it and supply the certificate only; keep the key private.
pemNeedsOne: A trust anchor is exactly one certificate. Remove the others.
pemNotCertificate: That does not look like a PEM certificate (it should start with BEGIN CERTIFICATE).
pemTooLarge: That is too large to be a certificate.
pemUnreadable: That file could not be read.
pinnedHint: The server computed this SHA-256 pin from the certificate. It is the credential's id, and it is public.
rotateNoSecret: This profile has no secret to rotate.
summaryNoteCertificate: Devices authenticate with a certificate chaining to the trust anchor, so there is no secret. A device earmarked for this profile takes its token from its certificate: {{prefix}} followed by the common name (its external id).
title: Trust anchors
